plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The solution space of a linear function is a 2-dimensional affine manifold; its rigidity arises from the invariance under affine transformations, meaning any set of $w \geq 3$ constraints uniquely determines the function, resulting in a minimal capacity $N_c \approx 2$ that remains flat as $w$ increases. | pro: This is the simplest rigid case with a clear algebraic ground truth, ensuring the bootstrap anchor is easily reachable and the trend is provably flat. It provides a necessary baseline for the capacity scan before testing more complex rigid or fat families. | con: It may be too trivial to provide deep insight into the generalization behavior of small networks compared to more complex rigid functions.

steps.description: Implement the family(kind, w, seed) function for the linear rigid family and the 20th-order polynomial fat family. This function must generate training points (X, y) and held-out points (Xv, yv) with shape (N, 1), normalize y/yv to O(1) scale, and ensure no overlap between X and Xv. The existing capacity_scan infrastructure will handle the two-layer tanh network training with L-BFGS-B.

[auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the family function for the two function classes (rigid linear and fat high-degree polynomial) ensuring correct output shapes (N,1), non-overlapping training/validation sets, and y/yv normalization to O(1) magnitude to validate the zero-violation criterion.
